summary: Maryla Falk was an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. She held a post at the University of Warsaw (~1936-1939) and was a member of the Polish Oriental Society (1938) and a Fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society (1974).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Sinology, Marylin Martin Rhie studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra. She served as a professor at Smith College (attested 1986).

Masaaki Chikusa was a scholar of Sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his degrees, including a doctorate (1980), at Kyoto University, later serving there as assistant professor (1968) and librarian-assistant (1981-1993), then professor at Otani University (~1994-2001).

Masaaki Hattori works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta under Naoshiro Tsuji and Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty posts at Kyoto University (1961-1988) and Hanazono University (~1993-1997).

Masaaki Nitta is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1983-1991) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).

Masaaki Noni is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Gadjin M. Nagao. He served as an assistant professor (attested 2003) and later as a professor (attested 2013-2014) at Ryukoku University.

Masaaki Sugiyama specialized in history and archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970-1980) and held a post at Kyoto Women's University (~1982-1992).
Masaaki Tsuchiya is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University (~1979-1988) and held a post at Senshu University around 1993.

Masaharu Anesaki worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Kiel University, and with scholars including Paul Deussen and Hermann Oldenberg. He held a professorship (1904) and served as library director (1923-1934) at the University of Tokyo.

Masaharu Imai specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He earned a doctorate from Tokyo University of Education (-1977) and served at Ibaraki University (1977) and the University of Tsukuba, where he became professor emeritus (2006).

Masahide Mori specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University and earned his PhD under Tadeusz Skorupski at SOAS University of London. His posts include assistant professor at Koyasan University (1994) and professor at Kanazawa University (~2007).
Masahiro Asada is a Buddhist studies scholar who was educated at Ryukoku University and later served there as an assistant professor (attested 1987).

Masahiro Inami specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed doctoral coursework at Hiroshima University (~1984-1989) and has held teaching posts at Tokyo Gakugei University (~1998; attested 2011-2016).

Masahiro Kusunoki was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1948-1953) and later served there as professor and chair of religious studies and the history of religion (attested 1980-1983).

Masahiro Shimoda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and doctorate at the University of Tokyo and studied at the University of Delhi. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1994-2023) and Musashino University (2023).
Masahiro Takano is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University and served as a librarian there (attested 1995).

Masakazu Tanaka is a scholar in religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University and earned his Ph.D. from the London School of Economics, University of London. He served at Kyoto University (1988-2019) and became vice president and professor at the Professional Institute of International Fashion (2019).

Masako Keta is a philosophy and religious studies scholar. She earned her degrees at Kyoto University under Yoshinori Takeuchi. She held posts at Kanazawa University (assistant professor 1988, professor 1998) and served as professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University (2000-2018).
Masamichi Asukai was a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. He completed his studies at Kyoto University (~1953-1957) and later served in an academic post there (~1968-1998).

Masamichi Ichigo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao. He served as professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (from 1981), Otani University (1997), and president of Kyoto Koka Women's University (2007).
